sections.overview: Biotoecus opercularis is a small geophagine cichlid native to the Amazon basin. Its congener B. dicentrarchus occurs in the Orinoco and has two anal-fin spines rather than three.
sections.identification: It has three anal-fin spines and a reported maximum total length near 10 cm. Compared with B. dicentrarchus, it has five rather than six dark flank blotches and a different lateral-line canal pattern.
sections.habitat: Its documented range includes the middle and lower Negro, Branco, Urubu and lower Trombetas rivers, plus Amazonian lakes and tributaries in Brazil. It is associated with shallow margins, sand and leaf litter in several types of Amazonian water.
sections.diet: The consulted sources do not provide a well-supported species-specific diet description. Its geophagine relatives often sift bottom material, but direct feeding observations are needed.
sections.behavior: Field and aquarium accounts describe a bottom-oriented dwarf cichlid of shallow river edges. Wild social behavior is not well quantified in the references used.
sections.reproduction: Reliable species-specific information on spawning and brood care was not found. Reproductive details should not be borrowed from B. dicentrarchus without evidence.
sections.ecology: It occupies the Amazon basin, unlike Orinoco-restricted B. dicentrarchus. Their anal-spine counts and flank markings help distinguish these two congeners.
sections.conservation: The sources establish a broad Brazilian Amazon range but do not verify a current global conservation category or population trend. Those status details remain unresolved.
